title: Left-click can never select a pipe or dismiss an open popover — handle_click_select is unreachable for non-node presses
detail: Only a node-snapped press sets drag.active, so the release branch — the sole caller of handle_click_select — never fires for pipe or ground presses. Pipe popovers (QoS dial, demolish) can never open; the advertised ground-click popover dismissal is dead.
recommended_fix: Run the select path on release regardless of drag: gate handle_click_select on press_node/press_valid (or !moved) instead of drag.active, keeping the draw-pipe branch gated on drag.

title: Hint strings from fmt.tprintf are stored in app.hint but the temp arena is freed at the top of every frame — use-after-free across the 2600ms TTL
detail: fmt.tprintf allocates on the temp arena, which free_all resets each frame; app.hint keeps a 2600 ms TTL, so draw_frame re-reads already-freed bytes for ~2.5 s and later tprintf calls can overwrite the region. Hint text renders stale or garbage.
recommended_fix: Copy hint strings into a persistent buffer owned by App (e.g. fixed [256]u8 + length) at set_hint time, or allocate with context.allocator and free on replacement.

title: TICK_SECONDS :: 0.1 is never referenced; comment claims it is derived from balance.logic_hz but the real value is computed elsewhere
evidence:
+TICK_SECONDS :: 0.1 // derived from balance.logic_hz at boot (catalog is the single source)
...
+	rc.driver.tick_seconds = 1.0 / f64(catalogs.balance.logic_hz)
detail: TICK_SECONDS appears exactly once in the diff (its declaration). The actual tick rate is computed in run_context_create from catalogs.balance.logic_hz, so the constant is dead and its comment misstates how the value is derived.
recommended_fix: Delete TICK_SECONDS, or derive it from catalogs.balance.logic_hz and use it in run_context_create so the constant and the runtime value cannot drift.

title: Grace countdown computes secs, discards it, and draws a static '!' — and the conversion is inverted (ticks × hz instead of ÷ hz)
evidence:
+	if snap.in_grace {
+		buf: [32]u8
+		secs := snap.grace_ticks_left * i32(v.catalogs.balance.logic_hz)
+		_ = secs
+		txt := fmt_bprintf(buf[:], "!", 0)
+		draw_text(v, txt, {x + w + 8, y}, 18, p.state_critical)
detail: The countdown seconds are computed (multiplying ticks by logic_hz — seconds need division by hz), immediately discarded via '_ = secs', and a static '!' is drawn instead. No countdown is ever displayed; the math is dead.
recommended_fix: Draw the actual remaining seconds (grace_ticks_left / logic_hz), or delete secs and the '_ =' escape line entirely.

title: autopilot_boot header promises the 'exact player path' through the command bus with action-log replay, but it mutates state via a testkit function
evidence:
+// houses) through the command bus — the exact player path, so autopilot runs
+// land in the action log and replay bit-for-bit.
...
+autopilot_boot :: proc(rc: ^Run_Context) {
+	pp.testkit_wire_boot(rc.state, rc.state.tick)
detail: autopilot_boot's body contains no Command construction and no action_log append — it calls pp.testkit_wire_boot directly on state. As written, the boot wiring bypasses the bus the header claims, so the replay claim is unsupported by this diff.
recommended_fix: Route boot wiring through bus_submit-style edits so it lands in action_log, or amend the header to state the testkit boot path is exempt from replay.

title: Unused local 'labels' in popover_click — dead code and a likely compile error (Odin rejects unused locals; the diff's own '_ = secs' shows the workaround)
detail: labels is declared and never read; the triage loop uses only i. The author's '_ = secs' in draw_health_meter shows unused locals must be silenced — this one has no silencing: dead code at minimum, possibly a build failure.
recommended_fix: Delete the labels declaration — the triage buttons are laid out and hit-tested by index only.

title: App.press_valid is written twice and never read anywhere in the diff
evidence:
+	press_valid: bool,
...
+		app.press = mouse
+		app.press_node = 0
+		app.press_valid = false
...
+			app.press_node = nid
+			app.press_valid = true
detail: press_valid is set to false then true in the press handler but has no read site in this chunk; press_node and drag.active carry the actual interaction state (and the release branch relies on drag.active).
recommended_fix: Remove the field, or use it to gate the release/select branch instead of drag.active.

title: The 'mark every live node wired' loop is duplicated in main.odin's A-key handler and autopilot_boot
detail: autopilot_boot already marks every live node wired before returning; the identical loop in the A-key handler is redundant and the two copies will drift if one changes.
recommended_fix: Keep only the loop inside autopilot_boot and drop the duplicate in main.odin.

title: Hud_State.time_ms and Hud_State.seed are populated every frame but never consumed
detail: draw_hud and every helper it calls consume only hud.hint and hud.onboarding; time_ms and seed are built into Hud_State on every frame and never read.
recommended_fix: Drop time_ms and seed from Hud_State (and the call site), or wire them into the pulse/era displays they were meant for.

title: start_run map generation always takes the hardcoded 1040×780 fallback on the first run, while R-key restarts use balance-derived view dims
evidence: +	app.map_gen = rnd.map_generate(app.seed, app.view.world_w == 0 ? 1040 : app.view.world_w, app.view.world_h == 0 ? 780 : app.view.world_h)
detail: start_run runs before any view_compute (world_w/h are 0 — view_compute only runs in handle_input), so run 1 always generates blobs for 1040×780 while R-key restarts use balance-derived dims; if those differ, the first map's geography sits in a mismatched space.
recommended_fix: Compute the view (or derive world dims from balance) before the first map_generate so every run uses the same coordinate space.

title: synth_sting's descending_alarm parameter is never used; the crisis sting's descending contour comes from the frequency list alone
detail: descending_alarm does not appear in synth_sting's body; the 660→415 sequence already descends via the freqs list, so the parameter and its true argument at the call site are dead.
recommended_fix: Remove the parameter, or implement the behavior it names (e.g. a per-note envelope/glide) so the flag shapes the sound.

title: draw_router puck sizing: integer division flattens ports 1–3, and the formula is always overridden by the if-chain for ports ≥ 8
evidence:
+	r := base * (0.85 + 0.15 * f32(max(1, n.ports) / 4))
+	if n.ports >= 16 { r = base * 1.35 } else if n.ports >= 8 { r = base * 1.1 }
detail: max(1, n.ports) / 4 is integer division, so routers with 1–3 ports render identically at 0.85×; and for ports ≥ 8 the computed r is unconditionally overwritten, making the formula dead exactly for the ports the chain covers.
recommended_fix: Use f32(max(1, n.ports)) / 4 and remove the if-chain, or keep the chain and delete the formula.
